text:
emily: Heads-up — Acme (tenant acme-corp) is hitting 504s + intermittent 5xx from hosted inference since ~14:02 UTC. Ticket #12345 opened by support. Customer sees long tail timeouts at the gateway and many retries.

raj: I can confirm gateway metrics show `request_queue_depth` pegged and p95 tail latency spiking. Continuous batching backlog appears to have grown.

carlos: Logs from gateway node gtw-12:```
2026-03-17T14:02:11Z ERROR gateway request timeout tenant=acme-corp route=/v1/generate id=9f3a status=504 queue_depth=1024
2026-03-17T14:02:12Z WARN batcher backlog=845 continuous_batching=true
2026-03-17T14:02:13Z ERROR model-serving kvcache-warmup ms=2200
```

sre-bot: alert:queue_depth_high host=gtw-12 metric=request_queue_depth value=1024 threshold=800

support-oncall: Customer repro steps in ticket: 1) send 300 r/s of short prompts (avg tokens=5) 2) repeated retries on 504 3) observed gateway timeouts after ~30s of sustained rate. They started after a deploy ~13:50 UTC but not sure if causal.

raj: Early hypothesis: high rate of tiny requests causes inefficient batching (small batch sizes) -> KV cache churn + model cold KV misses -> batcher stalls -> queue piles up. Also hitting per-host queue depth limit, which triggers early rejects/timeouts.

emily: Can we do quick mitigations? Options: 1) disable continuous batching for tenant, 2) raise queue depth on a few gateway nodes, 3) route acme-corp to a lower-latency fallback model variant or dedicated pool.

carlos: I just executed a scoped config change to turn off continuous batching for the tenant via admin console (ui) and `rictl tenants patch acme-corp --continuous_batching=false`. Will watch metrics.

deploy-bot: config-change: tenant=acme-corp continuous_batching=false by carlos at 2026-03-17T14:12:05Z

sre-bot: monitoring: queue_depth on gtw-12 fell from 1024 -> 420 over next 60s after config flip. 5xx rate dropping.

raj: Good sign. Can we also increase `request_queue_limit` on gtw-12 and gtw-13 temporarily to 2048 to avoid early rejects while we stabilize? Note: this increases memory pressure.

carlos: I can bump the limit on the two nodes but prefer cautious approach. Will increase on gtw-13 only for now: `kubectl patch cm gateway-config -n prod --patch '{"data":{"request_queue_limit":"2048"}}'` and restart pods via `kubectl rollout restart ds/gateway -n prod`.

emily: Please do gtw-13. Also open a canary route for acme-corp to set model_variant=small-quant and monitor quality. If latency acceptable, we can keep fallback.

carlos: gtw-13 patched and restarted. Rolling pods back up.

sre-bot: telemetry update: error rate for acme-corp decreased from 12% -> 2.1% within 3 minutes; p95 latency dropped from 2.9s -> 850ms.

support-oncall: Customer confirmed improvement in ticket. They still see occasional 504s during bursts but much better.

raj: Root cause follow-ups: 1) workload pattern (spiky tiny-requests) + continuous batching interaction 2) gating on KV cache warmup cost 3) per-host queue limits causing hard timeouts.

emily: Action items: - short: document per-tenant toggle & runbook (I updated runbook link in ticket) - medium: product to add adaptive batching settings per-tenant + auto-fallback to smaller model variant under queue pressure - infra: evaluate queue depth distribution and memory safety for temporary bumps - postmortem owner? @carlos can you take P0 postmortem and include timeline + repro?

carlos: I'll own the postmortem. Will capture exact repro with a load generator and add steps to reproduce on staging.

sre-bot: reminder: create incident epic and link ticket #12345, add `priority:high` label.

support-oncall: Marking customer ticket as updated with mitigation and ETA for postmortem. Customer asks for ETA on avoiding regression; provide them with current mitigations and next steps.

emily: Thanks all. Follow-up: schedule a 30m triage tomorrow to discuss longer-term controls (adaptive batching, per-tenant rate shaping). I'll ping product and infra. :thumbsup:
